newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips restructures TV operations in Belgium, France, Italy.
newsitem.headline: Philips restructures TV operations in Belgium, France, Italy.

text.p: Dutch group Philips Electronics NV said Thursday it is restructuring its television operations in Belgium, France and Italy in 1997, resulting in the loss of about 1,400 or half the jobs in those countries.
The move is part of a previously announced restructuring of Philips' sound and vision unit.
The three plants -- at Bruges in Belgium, Dreux in France and Monza in Italy -- are involved in manufacturing and development.

The restructuring changes mean Monza will stop its activities in mid-1997, while Bruges will be the worldwide high-end colour television development centre with a production facility, and Dreux will be the final assembly centre for western Europe.
Dreux will also have a limited development capacity for the regional adaptations of global product platforms.
Philips has already announced a restructuring of plants in Krefeld and Nuremburg in Germany; Dendermonde in Belgium and Vienna in Austria.
Witht the latest restructuring, some 2,500 jobs are being cut in the division's industrial activities in western Europe.

In marketing and sales, some 850 jobs in 16 European countries have been cut, while 350 research and development jobs are also going. Together with 150 jobs in staff departments the total western European job cuts will be around 3,900.
Philips said the sound and vision restructuring process was on schedule, while further initiatives were being prepared for its operations in the rest of the world.
Philips employs 270,000 people in 60 countries. The consumer products division, which includes sound and vision, had a total workforce of over 70,000 at the end of June.
